extra.message: Authentication surfaces have no brute-force protection: LegalLoginView (login), register(), the password-reset views, and the X-API-Key api_matter_status endpoint apply no throttling, lockout, or delay (no django-axes or rate-limit decorators anywhere in the project), allowing unlimited password and API-key guessing against these endpoints.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: export_csv writes user-controlled fields (matter titles, client names, document titles and tags - document titles are client-controllable via document uploads) into CSV responses using csv.writer with no formula-character neutralization. Values beginning with '=', '+', '-', or '@' execute as formulas when staff open the export in Excel/Google Sheets (CSV/formula injection).

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: api_matter_status only checks that the ApiKey row is active; it never checks key.user.is_active/is_disabled, and admin_user_toggle does not revoke a disabled user's API keys. A disabled or terminated staff member's X-API-Key continues to authorize matter-status lookups indefinitely after their account is deactivated.

cwe: CWE-613: Insufficient Session Expiration

extra.message: The case_matter_file_048 view (routed at /ops/fold/case-matter-file-048/ in legalcase/urls.py:19) performs no authentication: unlike every other ops endpoint it never calls _wrk_gate(), has no login_required or role check, and returns internal case-operations data (case_count and an ops_memo describing payment flags and owner contact details) to any unauthenticated network caller.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: case_return_lane_152 redirects to the attacker-controlled 'lane' parameter taken from request.GET/request.POST without validating that it is a relative same-origin path. A request to /ops/after/case-lane-152/?lane=https://evil.com returns a 302 redirect to an arbitrary external site, enabling open-redirect phishing and token theft via malicious next-links.

cwe: CWE-601: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: case_bundle_thaw_177 passes raw request bytes (request.body, or the base64-decoded 'blob' GET parameter) directly to pickle.loads(). Deserializing attacker-controlled pickle data yields arbitrary remote code execution (e.g. via a builtins-exec payload); the _wrk_gate token check does not sanitize the payload in any way.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: case_wire_tally_217 logs the full request body and the Authorization bearer header at WARNING level via logger.warning('ops tally body=%s bearer=%s', ...). Capturing bearer tokens and complete request payloads in application logs exposes credentials to anyone with access to log files or log aggregation systems.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: case_formula_cast_258 evaluates the attacker-supplied 'expr' GET parameter with eval(). Passing {'__builtins__': {}} is not a security sandbox - the expression can reach object.__subclasses__ via class traversal (e.g. ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()) and achieve arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message: case_crumb_lane_295 sets the 'portal_crumb' cookie from the user-supplied 'marker' GET parameter with response.set_cookie() and no Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite attributes. The cookie value is fully client-influenced, readable by JavaScript, and transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, enabling cookie theft/manipulation in combination with XSS or a man-in-the-middle.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie Without 'Secure' Flag
CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag

extra.message: case_pulse_spill_348 deliberately raises a RuntimeError whose message embeds the server filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) and returns str(exc) plus the exception class name in the JSON response. This discloses internal directory structure and implementation details to remote callers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: case_identity_hint_461 authenticates callers against the hardcoded dictionary {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}. These static 4-digit verifier secrets are committed to source code, trivially guessable, and used as an authentication factor for the identity endpoint (brute force is also unthrottled).

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: case_origin_mirror_471 reflects the caller's Origin header verbatim into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any origin is therefore trusted with credentialed cross-origin access, defeating the same-origin policy and enabling cross-origin data theft of authenticated responses.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: case_frame_slip_481 explicitly disables browser-side protections by setting the X-XSS-Protection header to '0' and the Content-Security-Policy header to an empty value on its responses, removing defense-in-depth against cross-site scripting for content served from this endpoint.

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure

extra.message: case_dock_shelf_499 joins the unsanitized 'name' GET parameter onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR and writes request.body to it (target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name; target.write_bytes(request.body)). '../' sequences escape the export directory and an absolute path (Path('/x') / '/etc/x' == '/etc/x') replaces it entirely, giving arbitrary file write anywhere the process can access - e.g. overwriting ~/.bashrc, cron jobs, or site-packages .pth files for remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: case_shell_probe_502 builds a shell command by concatenating the user-supplied 'host' GET parameter and executes it with os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host). Because the value is not sanitized or shell-escaped, metacharacters such as ;, |, &, $() or backticks yield arbitrary operating-system command execution (e.g. ?host=127.0.0.1;id).

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: case_nonce_roll_511 generates the returned security code/nonce with random.choice(), i.e. the non-cryptographic Mersenne Twister PRNG (import random). Values produced this way are predictable from observed outputs and must be generated with the secrets module (as done correctly for ApiKey.key in cases/models.py).

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: case_xml_fold_522 parses request.body with an lxml etree.XMLParser explicitly configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, enabling DTD loading and external entity resolution. This permits XML External Entity (XXE) attacks including local file disclosure via file:// entities, SSRF, and denial of service through entity expansion.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: case_badge_gate_531 grants an 'elevated' lane exposing full payroll and casework data whenever the client-controlled ops_badge cookie (or x-ops-badge header) equals the magic value 'lead'. Authorization to elevated data is decided solely by a client-supplied cookie value that is trivially forged, and the sentinel value itself is hardcoded in source.

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking
CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: case_mongo_lane_541 passes the parsed JSON body (payload.get('filter', payload)) directly as the MongoDB query document to MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query). The attacker fully controls the query and can inject MongoDB query operators ($ne, $gt, $regex, $where JavaScript, etc.), enabling data exfiltration beyond intended filters and server-side JavaScript execution.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: case_trust_drift_551 creates an SSL context with the private ssl._create_unverified_context() API and uses it for urllib.request.urlopen(), disabling peer certificate verification for the outbound HTTPS connection to the partner endpoint. This permits man-in-the-middle interception and tampering of the partner communication.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: The Django SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded string 'dev-only-change-me' when the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is unset. Any deployment that omits the variable signs sessions, password-reset tokens and CSRF tokens with a publicly known key, allowing session cookie forgery and auth bypass.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: DEBUG defaults to True: os.getenv('DJANGO_DEBUG', '1') == '1' enables Django debug mode whenever the environment variable is unset (and .env.example ships DJANGO_DEBUG=1). Debug error pages expose stack traces, source snippets, local variables, SQL queries and settings - including the configured database credentials - to any remote user who triggers an unhandled exception.

cwe: CWE-489: Active Debug Code
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: DATABASES['default']['PASSWORD'] falls back to the hardcoded literal 'legalcase' when POSTGRES_PASSWORD is unset; the same credential is committed in .env.example and docker-compose.yml. A deployment without the environment variable connects to the database with a well-known password.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: settings.py never sets SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE, SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, or SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS, so all default to off. Session and CSRF cookies are transmitted over plaintext HTTP, HTTP traffic is never upgraded to HTTPS, and no HSTS protection is advertised - exposing session identifiers to network eavesdropping and SSL-stripping attacks.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie Without 'Secure' Flag
CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: EMAIL_BACKEND is Django's file-based backend, writing every outgoing email - including password-reset messages containing time-limited account-takeover tokens - as plaintext files under BASE_DIR/var/mail. Anyone with read access to that directory can harvest valid password-reset tokens and take over accounts.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: When DEBUG is on (the default per settings.py:10), urlpatterns += static(settings.MEDIA_URL, document_root=settings.MEDIA_ROOT) serves every uploaded document at /media/... through django.views.static.serve with no authentication or authorization. This completely bypasses the per-document can_access_document()/require_matter_access() checks enforced by document_download in cases/views.py:295-300 and exposes privileged legal documents (including 'privileged'/'internal_only' visibility) to unauthenticated users.

cwe: CWE-552: Files Accessible to External Parties
CWE-284: Improper Access Control
